subject: Throughput sizing follow-up - FinEx (post-call)
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finex.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finex.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput sizing follow-up - FinEx (post-call)

Alex - thanks for the 30-minute sync this morning. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size Dedicated/Hosted options for your workload.

Recap:
- Primary use: API for document summarization + chat for customer support workflows.
- SLO targets: p95 latency target ~ 300ms for single-doc summarization, p99 TBD for large summarizations.
- Need streaming for partial responses in chat workflows.
- Security: SOC 2 required; will discuss Private deployment later in procurement track.

Items we need to finalize sizing (can you confirm / fill in):
1) QPS: peak and steady-state (e.g., 95th percentile steady QPS vs peak bursts).
2) Avg tokens/request and distribution (short vs long): mean, median, and 95th token lengths.
3) Concurrency: estimated simultaneous open sessions and concurrent decode ops.
4) Streaming requirements: percent of requests that must be streamed vs non-streaming.
5) Any per-customer rate limiting or multi-tenant isolation needs.

If you can drop the workload spreadsheet you referenced in the call, Marissa and I will produce a first-pass throughput estimate and GPU recommendation.

Next steps:
- Alex: send workload spreadsheet (tokens per request, hourly QPS profile)
- Redwood: return sizing + cost estimate in 48 business hours after receipt

Thanks - Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@finex.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up - FinEx (post-call)

Thanks Rafael - attaching the worksheet (finex_workload_summary.xlsx). Below are the numbers we have today - some are approximations but should be close enough for sizing.

Summary numbers (current prod traffic):
- Peak QPS (5-10 min bursts): 120 QPS
- Steady-state QPS (95th percentile hourly): 30 QPS
- Avg tokens per request: 250 tokens (median 180, 95th ~ 1,200 for long summarizations)
- Percent of requests requiring streaming: ~35% (chat streams where agents see partial results)
- Concurrent open sessions: ~1,000 active sessions, but concurrent decode ops (requests actively decoding) around 400 at peak
- Typical request types: 70% single-shot summarize, 30% multi-turn chat (avg 3 turns)

Derived tokens/sec (approx):
- Peak tokens/sec = 120 QPS * 250 tok = 30,000 tok/sec
- Steady tokens/sec (95th) = 30 QPS * 250 = 7,500 tok/sec

Latency SLOs we care about: p95 <= 300ms for single-shot summaries (the 95% bucket is customer-facing); p99 ideally < 1s but we accept higher for long summarizations (>1k tokens).

Attached: finex_workload_summary.xlsx (hourly QPS by day, token distribution)

Let us know if you need any other distribution data.

- Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of AI Platform, FinEx
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up - FinEx (post-call)

Alex - got it, thanks for the worksheet and the quick summary. A few clarifying Qs so our sizing is accurate:

1) Token distribution: can you add a simple histogram buckets (0-128, 129-512, 513-1024, >1024) and approximate % in each? The 95th at 1.2k suggests a non-trivial tail and will affect memory/KV cache sizing.
2) Streaming: of the 35% streaming requests, are those long-polling (i.e., streaming lasts >2s) or short-progressive (<1s)? This affects batching and latency guarantees.
3) Concurrency: when you say 400 concurrent decode ops at peak, is that observed during the 120 QPS bursts? Or is decode concurrency decoupled (e.g., many open websockets but fewer simultaneous decodes)?
4) Rate limiting: do you want per-customer QPS caps or a single shared pool? If multi-tenant per-customer caps are required we recommend reserved concurrency windows.

Preliminary sizing notes from Marissa (cc) and me: using an Llama-2-70B-style variant with bfloat16 / 4-bit quantization assumptions, a rough thumb estimate for the peak tokens/sec above (30k tok/s) suggests we should evaluate both Dedicated with 8 x H100 (inference-optimized configs) and Hosted with autoscaling + warm pools. We'll produce a more concrete GPU estimate once we see the histogram and concurrency shape.

If you can drop the small histogram and confirm the streaming latency profile, we'll aim to return a PDF estimate (redwood_throughput_estimate.pdf) with two options (Dedicated monthly commit vs Hosted burstable) by end of day Thursday.

Thanks - Rafael
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finex.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up - FinEx (post-call)

Adding a quick internal note on assumptions so the team knows the sizing path:

Assumptions we will model in the estimate:
- Model family: Llama-2-70B-ish (decoder-only) with quantized weights; inference perf baseline ~ 5-8 tok/ms per H100 GPU depending on kernels and seq length.
- Batch policy: continuous batching for short requests; streaming flag will reduce batching window for ~35% of traffic.
- KV cache: enabled for multi-turn; assume average context window of 2,048 tokens for multi-turn flows - this impacts GPU memory and how many sessions can be resident.
- Safety margin: include 25% headroom for burst capacity and autoscaling delays.

Prelim capacity sketches (very rough):
- Hosted (autoscale warm pool): to hit p95 < 300ms for single-shot at steady 30 QPS, a warm pool of 1-2 H100-equivalent nodes + autoscale to ~6-8 nodes at peak could be viable depending on batching effectiveness.
- Dedicated (committed): for predictable 120 QPS bursts and 30k tok/sec peak, 6-8 H100s with optimized kernels and aggressive batching looks like the right starting point; we'll refine after token-bucket histogram.

I'll produce a numerical table in the PDF estimate once we have the histogram and confirm streaming durations.

- Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>; Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up - FinEx (post-call)

Thanks Rafael/Marissa - quick answers below and I attached the histogram tab in the spreadsheet as requested.

Histogram buckets (approx %):
- 0-128 tokens: 40%
- 129-512 tokens: 45%
- 513-1024 tokens: 10%
- >1024 tokens: 5%

Streaming profile: ~25% of streaming requests are long-lived (>2s streaming); the rest are short progressive updates (~0.5-1s). Yes, the 400 concurrent decodes was during the 120 QPS peak window.

Rate limiting: initially shared pool; may add per-customer caps in Q4.

Happy to meet Thursday AM if that helps - otherwise we'll wait for the PDF estimate.

- Alex
